To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tα1 and to a lesser extent T26 α-tuublin transcripts were differentially expressed in cerebellar granular cells in vitro and that Tα1 mRNA levels were correlated with neuritogenesis.
the two α-tubulin genes, Tα1 and β3-tubulin, have different expression profiles during the development of cultured cerebellum.

the two α-tubulin isotypes, Tα1 and the T26, are expressed in a cell-type specific manner in the developing rat brain, that Tα1 is associated with neuritogenesis, and that Tα26 is associated with cell proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of α-tubulins during neuronal development.
the regulation of tubulin gene expression during neuronal differentiation.
the regulation of tubulin gene expression in developing neurons, particularly in cerebellar granules, and the possible role of tubulin isotypes in the differentiation of these cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tα1 and β-tubulin are the most important tubulins in the assembly of neuronal microtubules, and Tα1 may be involved in the neuritogenesis and/or the axon formation.
the T26 mRNA is expressed at a high level during the early phase of cell proliferation and is maintained at a high level throughout the cell cycle.
the T26 transcript is constitutive and may be related to cell proliferation, whereas the Tα1 mRNA is developmentally regulated and may be related specifically to neuronal differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Tα1 and βIII tubulin are the major α- and β-tubulin isotypes expressed in neurons and that their differential expression during neuronal development is a result of the regulation of their respective mRNAs.
α-tubulin expression in the developing cerebellum is under complex developmental regulation and the different α-tubulin isotypes may play different roles in neuronal development.
α-tubulin expression during neuronal differentiation is complex and may be regulated at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Tα1 and β-tubulin m RNA expression is developmentally regulated during the differentiation of cerebellar granular cells and is consistent with a role for Tα1 and its associated microtubule network in neuritogenesis.
α-tubulins are differentially regulated in neurons and that this differential regulation is likely to be important for the function of neurons.
Tα1 is a marker of neurite outgrowth, while T26 is associated with cell proliferation.
